import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Map 'is_fraud' column for better readability in plots
df['is_fraud_label'] = df['is_fraud'].map({0: 'Legitimate', 1: 'Fraudulent'})

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes for a 1x3 layout
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(22, 7))
fig.suptitle('Credit Card Transaction Analysis: Fraud vs. Legitimate Transactions', fontsize=18, y=1.02) # y adjusts title position

# Plot 1: Distribution of Transaction Amount by Fraud Status
sns.kdeplot(data=df, x='amount', hue='is_fraud_label', fill=True, ax=axes[0], palette='viridis', common_norm=False)
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Amount', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
axes[0].legend(title='Fraud Status', title_fontsize='11', fontsize='10')

# Plot 2: Transaction Count by Hour of Day and Fraud Status
# Using histplot with 'dodge' to clearly separate legitimate and fraudulent counts
sns.histplot(data=df, x='hour_of_day', hue='is_fraud_label', multiple='dodge', bins=24, ax=axes[1], palette='viridis', shrink=0.8)
axes[1].set_title('Transaction Count by Hour of Day', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day (0-23)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Number of Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_xticks(range(0, 24, 2)) # Set ticks for every 2 hours
axes[1].legend(title='Fraud Status', title_fontsize='11', fontsize='10')

# Plot 3: Transaction Type Counts by Fraud Status
sns.countplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', hue='is_fraud_label', ax=axes[2], palette='viridis')
axes[2].set_title('Transaction Type Counts', fontsize=14)
axes[2].set_xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=12)
axes[2].set_ylabel('Number of Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[2].legend(title='Fraud Status', title_fontsize='11', fontsize='10')
axes[2].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=15) # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability if needed

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/titles from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.96]) # Adjust rect to make space for the main suptitle

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
